key_insight: Learning to sample from a soft-optimal Gibbs distribution is statistically different from finding a single best action, and this shift can reduce regret from O(\sqrt{T}) to logarithmic in T under standard conditions.
engineering_relevance: For RLHF, entropy-regularized RL, and reward-guided generation, the paper provides a principled way to optimize diverse high-quality outputs instead of only maximizing top-1 accuracy.
method: Defines sampling regret as temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence to the Gibbs target.
Derives unified regret decompositions showing sampling regret depends on squared confidence widths rather than first-order uncertainty.
Introduces sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling: UCS and TS^2, including a Bayesian decomposition for posterior-random Gibbs distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret guarantees and unified decompositions rather than an empirical benchmark, with logarithmic-in-T sampling regret at fixed temperature in standard settings.
watch_item: The logarithmic regret gains rely on fixed-temperature assumptions and problem-specific uncertainty structure, so performance may degrade if the target distribution or reward model shifts substantially.
paper_title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
